# Overview
The Bayesian-ECD Shiny application provides a graphical interface for Bayesian survival analysis that incorporates information from external control data (ECD) into the analysis of a current randomized clinical trial (RCT). The application is designed to make the Bayesian-ECD historical-borrowing workflow accessible to trial investigators by providing posterior survival and treatment-effect estimation, restricted mean survival time (RMST) summaries, prespecified subpopulation analyses, and prediction in new patient populations.

The application uses stored posterior information from the historical Bayesian-ECD model together with an uploaded current RCT dataset. Users provide the required column names and covariates through the Shiny interface, after which the application performs the Bayesian-ECD analysis and provides graphical and numerical summaries of treatment-specific survival.

## Software Availability

The Bayesian-ECD Shiny application, source code, example datasets, analysis utilities, and current user documentation are available through the **[Bayesian-ECD-Shiny GitHub repository](https://github.com/bhngrg/Bayesian-ECD-Shiny)**.

The main workflow is:

1. **Upload the current RCT dataset** and specify the columns containing the patient ID, overall survival outcome, censoring indicator, treatment, cohort, and required baseline covariates.
2. **Optionally assess control compatibility** when the current RCT contains a concurrent control arm labeled `Control`. This diagnostic compares the observed concurrent-control survival experience with the historical Bayesian-ECD posterior predictive control distribution.
3. **Examine the primary Bayesian-ECD results**, including treatment-specific survival curves, time-varying hazard-ratio curves, and RMST summaries.
4. **Perform subpopulation analyses** by restricting the analysis according to baseline patient characteristics such as sex, extent of resection (EOR), Karnofsky Performance Status (KPS), and age.
5. **Optionally upload a new covariate-only dataset** to obtain survival predictions and RMST summaries for a new target population.
6. **Optionally perform posterior-probability analyses outside the Shiny interface** using the utilities provided in the repository.

The application also provides download options for plots, RMST tables, and selected Bayesian-ECD model results.

> **Note:** The control compatibility diagnostic is optional. A concurrent control arm is not required to proceed with the primary Bayesian-ECD analysis.


# Installation and Launch

The Bayesian-ECD Shiny application runs locally in R and requires **R version 4.2.2 or later**. The repository contains the Shiny application, supporting R and C++ functions, stored Bayesian-ECD model components, example datasets, and optional analysis utilities.

## Download the Repository

The repository can be obtained by cloning it with Git:

```bash
git clone https://github.com/bhngrg/Bayesian-ECD-Shiny.git
cd Bayesian-ECD-Shiny
```

Alternatively, the repository can be downloaded from GitHub as a ZIP archive and extracted to a local directory.

## Install Required R Packages

The application requires several R packages for the Shiny interface, data processing, plotting, parallel computation, statistical analysis, and compilation of the supporting C++ code.

Install the required packages from the R console:

```r
install.packages(c(
  "shiny",
  "bslib",
  "tibble",
  "dplyr",
  "readr",
  "ggplot2",
  "reshape2",
  "plyr",
  "foreach",
  "doParallel",
  "matrixStats",
  "DT",
  "patchwork",
  "gridExtra",
  "gt",
  "writexl",
  "zip",
  "Rcpp",
  "RcppArmadillo",
  "RcppDist",
  "purrr",
  "rstudioapi",
  "mcclust",
  "cluster",
  "e1071",
  "randomForest",
  "survival"
))
```

The application includes C++ code that is compiled at runtime using `Rcpp::sourceCpp()`, with `RcppArmadillo` and `RcppDist` used by the underlying C++ implementation. Most users will receive precompiled R package binaries, but appropriate system build tools may be required if R installs packages from source.

### macOS

Install the Xcode Command Line Tools from Terminal:

```bash
xcode-select --install
```

On Apple Silicon Macs, GNU Fortran may also be required when R compiles packages containing Fortran code. If package installation produces errors involving `gfortran`, Fortran, or `-lgfortran`, install the GNU Fortran tools appropriate for your version of R.

### Windows

Install the version of Rtools corresponding to your installed version of R if package compilation is required.

### Ubuntu/Debian Linux

Install the standard build tools and development libraries:

```bash
sudo apt-get update
sudo apt-get install build-essential libcurl4-openssl-dev libssl-dev libxml2-dev
```

## Launch the Application

The recommended approach is to open the repository in RStudio and run the application from there.

The complete repository should contain directories such as:

```text
app/
app_core/
analysis_utils/
example_data/
examples/
docs/
```

Open `app/app.R` in RStudio and select:

**Run App > Run in Window**

Alternatively, from the R console, set the working directory to the **root of the repository** and run:

```r
shiny::runApp("app")
```

When the application starts, the **Uploaded Data** tab is the starting point for the primary Bayesian-ECD workflow.

> **Important:** Run the application from the complete repository. The Shiny application depends on supporting functions and stored model components located outside `app/app.R`.


# Preparing the Current RCT Dataset

The primary Bayesian-ECD analysis begins with a CSV file containing the current RCT data. The application asks the user to identify the columns containing the survival outcome, treatment information, and baseline covariates used by the model.

An example model-fitting dataset is provided in:

```text
example_data/example_model_data.csv
```

The example dataset contains 300 patients and the following columns:

| Column | Description |
|---|---|
| `ID` | Patient identifier |
| `age` | Baseline age in years |
| `os` | Overall survival time in days |
| `os_status` | Event/censoring indicator |
| `trt` | Treatment assignment |
| `sex` | Sex |
| `kps` | Baseline Karnofsky Performance Status (KPS) category |
| `eor` | Extent of resection (EOR) category |
| `cohort` | Cohort/source indicator |

The user's column names do not need to match these example names. Instead, the corresponding column names are entered in the **Uploaded Data** tab before the CSV file is submitted.

## Required Information

The **Uploaded Data** tab asks the user to identify the following variables.

### Patient ID

Specify the column containing the patient identifier. Patient identifiers may contain numbers, letters, or a combination of both.

For the example dataset:

```text
ID
```

### Overall Survival

Specify the column containing overall survival time in days.

For the example dataset:

```text
os
```

Overall survival should represent the time from the relevant study origin to death or last follow-up.

### Censoring Indicator

Specify the column containing the event/censoring indicator.

For the example dataset:

```text
os_status
```

The application expects:

```text
TRUE  = death/event observed
FALSE = censored/alive at last follow-up
```

### Treatment

Specify the column containing the treatment assignment.

For the example dataset:

```text
trt
```

The reference control treatment must be labeled exactly:

```text
Control
```

Other treatment labels may identify the experimental treatment arms in the current RCT.

The exact `Control` label is particularly important if the optional **Control Compatibility** diagnostic will be used.

### Cohort

Specify the column identifying the cohort or data source.

For the example dataset:

```text
cohort
```

The application supports one current trial dataset at a time, so the current RCT cohort column should contain one cohort value.

### Age

Specify the column containing baseline age in years.

For the example dataset:

```text
age
```

The application interface recommends ages between approximately 21 and 81.22 years.

### Sex

Specify the column containing sex.

For the example dataset:

```text
sex
```

The uploaded dataset should use the category labels:

```text
Female
Male
```

The application matches these labels to the categorical level structure stored in the historical Bayesian-ECD model. Internally, the matched categories are converted to 0-based numeric codes for model computation.

### Karnofsky Performance Status

Specify the column containing the baseline KPS category.

For the example dataset:

```text
kps
```

The uploaded dataset should use the KPS category labels:

```text
> 80
(60, 80]
<= 60
```

These labels are matched to the categorical levels stored in the historical Bayesian-ECD model before being converted internally for model computation.

### Extent of Resection

Specify the column containing the extent-of-resection category.

For the example dataset:

```text
eor
```

The uploaded dataset should use the EOR category labels:

```text
GTR
STR
biopsy
```

where `GTR` denotes gross total resection and `STR` denotes subtotal resection. These labels are matched to the categorical levels stored in the historical Bayesian-ECD model before being converted internally for model computation.

## Uploading the Dataset

After entering the required column names in the **Uploaded Data** tab:

1. Click **Choose CSV File**.
2. Select the current RCT dataset in CSV format.
3. Verify that the entered column names correspond exactly to columns in the uploaded file.
4. Click **Submit**.

The uploaded dataset is displayed in the main panel of the **Uploaded Data** tab so that the data can be reviewed before proceeding to the analysis outputs.

> **Important:** The column names entered in the application must match the corresponding column names in the uploaded CSV file.

> **Important:** Categorical values in the uploaded RCT must match the category labels represented in the stored historical Bayesian-ECD model. The application aligns uploaded categories to the stored Stage 1 level structure and will report an error if an unseen category is encountered.


# Optional Control Compatibility Check

The **Control Compatibility** tab provides an optional diagnostic for assessing whether the concurrent control patients in the current RCT appear compatible with the historical control information represented by the Bayesian-ECD model.

This diagnostic is available when the uploaded current RCT dataset contains a concurrent control arm. The control treatment must be labeled exactly:

```text
Control
```

A concurrent control arm is **not required** to use the primary Bayesian-ECD analysis. If no patients labeled `Control` are present, the compatibility diagnostic cannot be performed, but the user may continue with the other analysis tabs.

## Purpose of the Diagnostic

The compatibility check compares the observed survival experience of the concurrent control patients with the historical Bayesian-ECD posterior predictive control distribution.

Only patients in the uploaded dataset whose treatment is labeled `Control` are included in the observed concurrent-control analysis. Uploaded experimental-treatment patients are not used. The historical posterior predictive control distribution is generated from the stored Bayesian-ECD posterior. The number of evaluable concurrent-control patients determines the sample size used when generating posterior predictive control-sample medians.

The diagnostic does not perform the Stage 2 Bayesian-ECD model extension used for the primary treatment analysis. Instead, it compares the observed current concurrent-control survival experience with the stored historical posterior predictive control distribution.

## Running the Compatibility Check

After the current RCT dataset has been uploaded and submitted in the **Uploaded Data** tab:

1. Open the **Control Compatibility** tab.
2. Confirm that the application has detected concurrent-control patients.
3. Select the minimum and maximum times to display in the diagnostic plot.
4. Click **Run compatibility check**.

If concurrent-control patients are available, the application reports how many were detected before the diagnostic is run. At least five concurrent-control patients with usable survival time and censoring information are required to perform the diagnostic.

The default plotting range is:

```text
Minimum time: 150 days
Maximum time: 1200 days
```

These values define the time window used to generate and retain the diagnostic survival curves and may be changed by the user.

## Diagnostic Output

The compatibility diagnostic compares two sources of information:

- the observed survival experience of the uploaded concurrent-control patients; and
- the historical Bayesian-ECD posterior predictive control distribution generated from the stored historical posterior.

The observed concurrent-control survival distribution is summarized using the Kaplan--Meier estimator.

The historical posterior predictive distribution is generated from the stored Bayesian-ECD posterior information.

The diagnostic displays the observed concurrent-control Kaplan–Meier curve with its 95% confidence interval together with the historical posterior predictive control curve and its 95% posterior interval.

It also compares the observed Kaplan–Meier median survival time with the posterior predictive distribution of control-sample medians. For each selected posterior draw, the application generates a predictive control sample with the same number of evaluable patients as the uploaded concurrent-control arm and calculates its sample median. The 95% posterior predictive interval of these simulated sample medians is used for the compatibility assessment.

## Interpreting the Compatibility Assessment

The diagnostic asks whether the observed concurrent-control median survival is consistent with the range of median survival values predicted from the historical Bayesian-ECD model.

If the observed Kaplan–Meier median falls within the 95% posterior predictive interval, the application reports the result as **Compatible**.

If the observed Kaplan–Meier median falls outside the 95% posterior predictive interval, the application reports **Potential incompatibility detected**.

If the observed Kaplan–Meier median is not reached, the application does not make the median-based compatibility determination and instead reports **Observed KM median not reached; review curve-level agreement**.

This assessment should be interpreted together with the displayed survival curves rather than solely as a binary decision.

> **Important:** The compatibility check is a diagnostic assessment. It does not prevent the user from continuing to the primary Bayesian-ECD analysis.

## Downloading the Compatibility Plot

The diagnostic plot can be saved using **Download Compatibility Plot (.png)**.

The user may optionally specify the desired plot width and height in inches before downloading. If custom dimensions are not supplied, the application uses a default download size of 14 × 8 inches.

# Primary Bayesian-ECD Outputs

After the current RCT dataset has been uploaded and the Bayesian-ECD analysis has been performed, the primary treatment-effect results can be examined using the **Plot Output** and **RMST Output** tabs.

These tabs allow the user to select a reference treatment and a comparison treatment. Treatment comparisons should therefore be interpreted relative to the treatment selected as the reference.

## Plot Output

The **Plot Output** tab provides graphical summaries of the Bayesian-ECD survival analysis.

### Selecting Treatments

Select:

1. the **reference treatment**; and
2. the **comparison treatment**.

For a comparison of an experimental treatment with the concurrent control arm, for example, `Control` would typically be selected as the reference treatment and the experimental treatment as the comparison treatment.

### Selecting a Plot

Two plot types are available:

- **Survival probabilities vs. Time (Days)**
- **Hazard Ratio vs. Time (Days)**

The minimum and maximum follow-up times used to generate the plotted estimates can be specified in days. The default range is:

```text
Minimum time: 150 days
Maximum time: 1200 days
```

After making the selections, click **Submit** to generate the requested plot.

### Survival Probability Plot

The survival probability plot displays the estimated treatment-specific survival probabilities over time for the selected reference and comparison treatments.

The curves summarize the Bayesian-ECD posterior survival estimates for the current RCT population and include 95% posterior intervals around the estimated survival probabilities.

This plot can be used to examine how the estimated survival experience differs between the selected treatments over the displayed follow-up period.

### Hazard-Ratio Plot

The hazard-ratio plot displays the estimated hazard ratio of the selected comparison treatment relative to the selected reference treatment as a function of time, with a 95% posterior interval. The hazard ratio is calculated as the hazard for the comparison treatment divided by the hazard for the reference treatment.

A horizontal reference line at a hazard ratio of 1 represents equal estimated hazards between the two treatments. Values above or below 1 should be interpreted according to the selected comparison and reference treatments.

Because the hazard ratio is estimated as a function of time, the treatment comparison is not summarized by a single constant hazard ratio.

## RMST Output

The **RMST Output** tab provides treatment comparisons based on restricted mean survival time (RMST).

RMST represents the expected survival time accumulated up to a specified time horizon. Unlike a hazard-ratio summary, RMST provides a treatment comparison directly on the survival-time scale.

### Selecting the RMST Comparison

Select:

1. the **reference treatment**;
2. the **comparison treatment**; and
3. the **RMST horizon time** in days.

The default horizon is:

```text
730.5 days
```

which corresponds to approximately two years.

After making the selections, click **Submit** to generate the RMST output.

### Interpreting the RMST Output

The RMST output summarizes the restricted mean survival time for each selected treatment through the specified horizon.

The output also provides two treatment-effect summaries:

- **RMST difference**, calculated as the RMST for the comparison treatment minus the RMST for the reference treatment; and
- **RMST ratio**, calculated as the RMST for the comparison treatment divided by the RMST for the reference treatment.

The treatment-specific RMST values are summarized by their posterior medians. The RMST difference and RMST ratio are reported using the 2.5th, 50th, and 97.5th posterior quantiles, corresponding to a 95% posterior interval. Users should therefore verify the treatment selections before interpreting the direction of an estimated treatment effect.

## Downloading Primary Results

Several outputs from the primary Bayesian-ECD analysis can be downloaded directly from the application.

From the **Plot Output** tab:

- **Download Plot (.png)** saves the currently selected Bayesian-ECD plot.
- **Download Bayesian-ECD Results (.zip)** saves selected model results used by the application.

The downloaded ZIP archive contains:

```text
picube.xlsx
Lognormal_Mu_Cube.xlsx
Lognormal_Sig_Cube.xlsx
Allocation_variables.xlsx
Variable_specifications.txt
```

From the **RMST Output** tab:

- **Download RMST Plot (.png)** saves the displayed RMST output.

For downloadable plots, the user may optionally specify the desired width and height in inches. If custom dimensions are not supplied, the displayed plot dimensions are used.

> **Important:** Always verify the selected reference and comparison treatments when interpreting treatment-effect quantities such as the hazard ratio, RMST difference, and RMST ratio.


# Subpopulation Analysis

The **Subpopulation Analysis** tab allows the primary Bayesian-ECD treatment comparisons to be evaluated within a patient subpopulation defined by selected baseline characteristics.

The user can define the subpopulation according to sex, extent of resection (EOR), Karnofsky Performance Status (KPS), and age. The resulting survival and hazard-ratio estimates are then calculated for patients meeting the selected criteria.

## Selecting Treatments and Plot Type

As in the primary **Plot Output** tab, select:

1. the **reference treatment**;
2. the **comparison treatment**; and
3. the desired plot type.

The available plot types are:

- **Survival probabilities vs. Time (Days)**
- **Hazard Ratio vs. Time (Days)**

The minimum and maximum follow-up times used to generate the plotted estimates can also be specified in days.

## Defining the Subpopulation

The subpopulation can be restricted using one or more of the following baseline characteristics.

### Sex

One or more of the following categories may be selected:

```text
Female
Male
```

### Extent of Resection

One or more EOR categories may be selected:

```text
GTR
STR
biopsy
```

where `GTR` denotes gross total resection and `STR` denotes subtotal resection.

### Karnofsky Performance Status

One or more KPS categories may be selected:

```text
> 80
(60, 80]
<= 60
```

### Age

The user specifies a minimum and maximum age in years.

The age interval is interpreted as:

```text
minimum age <= age < maximum age
```

Therefore, the minimum age is included and the maximum age is excluded.

For example:

```text
Minimum age: 48
Maximum age: 81
```

includes patients who are 48 years old but excludes patients who are 81 years old.

The application currently recommends keeping the selected age range within approximately 21 to 81.22 years.

## Running the Subpopulation Analysis

After selecting the treatments, plot type, follow-up range, and desired subpopulation characteristics, click **Submit**.

The application identifies the patients satisfying the specified restrictions and generates the requested Bayesian-ECD survival or hazard-ratio plot for that subpopulation. The survival and hazard-ratio plots summarize the corresponding posterior estimates with 95% posterior intervals. The hazard ratio is calculated as the hazard for the comparison treatment divided by the hazard for the reference treatment.

The displayed plot also reports the number of patients included in the selected subpopulation.

If the selected criteria result in zero or one patient, the application reports that the selected subpopulation is too small for a meaningful analysis.

## Subpopulation RMST Output

The **Subpopulation RMST Output** tab provides RMST summaries for the same patient subpopulation selected in the **Subpopulation Analysis** tab.

First define and submit the desired patient subpopulation in the **Subpopulation Analysis** tab. Then open the **Subpopulation RMST Output** tab and specify the RMST horizon time.

The default horizon is:

```text
730.5 days
```

which corresponds to approximately two years.

Click **Submit** to generate the RMST table.

The resulting table summarizes the treatment-specific RMST estimates and the corresponding RMST difference and RMST ratio for the selected reference and comparison treatments within the defined subpopulation. The RMST difference is calculated as the RMST for the comparison treatment minus the RMST for the reference treatment, and the RMST ratio is calculated as the comparison-treatment RMST divided by the reference-treatment RMST. The table reports the 2.5th, 50th, and 97.5th posterior quantiles, corresponding to a 95% posterior interval.

> **Important:** The **Subpopulation RMST Output** uses the treatment and patient-subpopulation selections made in the **Subpopulation Analysis** tab.

## Downloading Subpopulation Results

From the **Subpopulation Analysis** tab:

- **Download Plot (.png)** saves the displayed subpopulation survival or hazard-ratio plot.

The user may optionally specify the desired plot width and height in inches before downloading.

From the **Subpopulation RMST Output** tab:

- **Download RMST Table (.csv)** saves the displayed subpopulation RMST results as a CSV file.

> **Important:** More restrictive combinations of sex, EOR, KPS, and age will reduce the number of patients contributing to the subpopulation analysis. The displayed subpopulation sample size should therefore be considered when interpreting the resulting estimates.

# Prediction in a New Population

The prediction workflow allows the fitted Bayesian-ECD model to be applied to a new target population. Users can upload a covariate-only dataset and obtain treatment-specific survival predictions, hazard-ratio estimates, and RMST summaries standardized to the baseline characteristics of that population.

An example prediction dataset is provided in:

```text
example_data/example_prediction_data.csv
```

The example dataset contains 150 patients and the following columns:

| Column | Description |
|---|---|
| `ID` | Patient identifier |
| `age` | Baseline age in years |
| `sex` | Sex |
| `kps` | Baseline Karnofsky Performance Status (KPS) category |
| `eor` | Extent of resection (EOR) category |

Unlike the current RCT dataset used for the primary analysis, the prediction dataset does not require observed survival time, censoring status, treatment assignment, or cohort information.

## Uploading Prediction Data

Open the **Prediction Data** tab after completing the primary Bayesian-ECD analysis.

Specify the column containing the patient identifier. For the example prediction dataset, this is:

```text
ID
```

The prediction dataset must contain the same baseline covariates used by the Bayesian-ECD model. Categorical values should use the same category labels represented in the stored historical Bayesian-ECD model. The application aligns prediction categories to the stored Stage 1 level structure and reports an error if an unseen category is encountered.

To upload the prediction dataset:

1. Enter the prediction patient-ID column name.
2. Click **Choose Prediction CSV File**.
3. Select the covariate-only prediction dataset in CSV format.
4. Click **Submit**.

The uploaded prediction dataset is displayed in the main panel so that it can be reviewed before generating predictions.

## Prediction Output

The **Prediction Output** tab generates treatment-specific predictions for the uploaded target population.

Select:

1. the **prediction reference treatment**;
2. the **prediction comparison treatment**; and
3. the desired plot type.

The available plot types are:

- **Survival probabilities vs. Time (Days)**
- **Hazard Ratio vs. Time (Days)**

The minimum and maximum follow-up times used to generate the plotted estimates can also be specified.

By default, predictions are generated using the full uploaded prediction population.

## Applying Subpopulation Filters

The prediction workflow can optionally be restricted to a subpopulation of the uploaded prediction dataset.

Select:

**Apply subpopulation filters to prediction dataset**

to enable filters for:

- sex;
- EOR;
- KPS; and
- age.

The categorical filters use the same categories as the primary subpopulation analysis.

For age, the interval is interpreted as:

```text
minimum age <= age < maximum age
```

so the minimum age is included and the maximum age is excluded.

When subpopulation filtering is enabled, the displayed plot reports the number of prediction patients included in the selected subpopulation. When filtering is not enabled, the displayed sample size corresponds to the full prediction dataset.

After making the desired selections, click **Submit** to generate the prediction plot.

## Interpreting Prediction Plots

The survival probability plot summarizes the treatment-specific survival distributions predicted for the uploaded target population under the selected treatments, with 95% posterior intervals.

The hazard-ratio plot summarizes the corresponding treatment comparison over time for that population, with a 95% posterior interval. The hazard ratio is calculated as the hazard for the comparison treatment divided by the hazard for the reference treatment.

These predictions are standardized to the baseline covariate distribution of the uploaded prediction dataset, or to the selected subpopulation when prediction filters are enabled.

The prediction workflow therefore allows the fitted Bayesian-ECD model to be evaluated for a target population whose baseline characteristics may differ from those of the current RCT dataset.

## Prediction RMST Output

The **Prediction RMST Output** tab provides RMST summaries for the same prediction population used in the **Prediction Output** tab.

Specify the desired RMST horizon time. The default is:

```text
730.5 days
```

which corresponds to approximately two years.

Click **Submit** to generate the prediction RMST table.

The resulting table provides treatment-specific RMST estimates together with the RMST difference and RMST ratio for the selected reference and comparison treatments. The RMST difference is calculated as the RMST for the comparison treatment minus the RMST for the reference treatment, and the RMST ratio is calculated as the comparison-treatment RMST divided by the reference-treatment RMST. The table reports the 2.5th, 50th, and 97.5th posterior quantiles, corresponding to a 95% posterior interval.

If subpopulation filtering was enabled in the **Prediction Output** tab, the RMST results correspond to that selected prediction subpopulation. Otherwise, they correspond to the full uploaded prediction dataset.

> **Important:** The **Prediction RMST Output** uses the treatment and population selections established in the **Prediction Output** tab.

## Downloading Prediction Results

From the **Prediction Output** tab:

- **Download Prediction Plot (.png)** saves the displayed prediction survival or hazard-ratio plot.

The user may optionally specify the desired plot width and height in inches before downloading.

From the **Prediction RMST Output** tab:

- **Download Prediction RMST Table (.csv)** saves the displayed prediction RMST results as a CSV file.

> **Important:** Prediction results describe model-based treatment-specific survival for the covariate distribution of the uploaded target population. The prediction dataset does not need observed outcomes or actual treatment assignments.

# Optional Posterior-Probability Analyses

In addition to the graphical and RMST summaries available through the Shiny application, the repository provides optional R utilities for calculating posterior probabilities for prespecified treatment-effect thresholds.

These analyses are performed outside the Shiny interface and are intended for users who want to evaluate posterior evidence for specific hazard-ratio or RMST criteria.

The utility functions are provided in:

```text
analysis_utils/posterior-probability-utils.R
```

A worked example is provided in:

```text
examples/run_posterior_probabilities.R
```

## Available Posterior-Probability Utilities

Two primary functions are available:

```r
posterior_prob_hr_lt()
```

and

```r
posterior_prob_rmst()
```

The first evaluates posterior probabilities for hazard-ratio thresholds, while the second evaluates posterior probabilities for RMST-based treatment comparisons.

Both utilities can be applied to the full analysis population or to a specified subpopulation.

## Hazard-Ratio Posterior Probability

The function:

```r
posterior_prob_hr_lt()
```

calculates the posterior probability that the hazard ratio for a selected comparison is below a prespecified threshold at a selected time point. The hazard ratio is calculated as the hazard for the comparison treatment divided by the hazard for the reference treatment.

Conceptually, the quantity of interest is:

$$
P(HR(t) < c \mid \text{data})
$$

where $t$ is the selected time point and $c$ is the user-specified hazard-ratio threshold.

For example, a user may evaluate the posterior probability that the hazard ratio at two years is below a clinically meaningful threshold.

The function also provides a posterior summary of the corresponding hazard-ratio distribution. By default, this summary reports the 2.5th, 50th, and 97.5th posterior quantiles, corresponding to a 95% posterior interval.

## RMST Posterior Probabilities

The function:

```r
posterior_prob_rmst()
```

calculates posterior probabilities for treatment comparisons based on restricted mean survival time.

The utility supports both the RMST difference and RMST ratio. The RMST difference is calculated as the RMST for the comparison treatment minus the RMST for the reference treatment, and the RMST ratio is calculated as the comparison-treatment RMST divided by the reference-treatment RMST.

For the RMST difference, users can evaluate a posterior probability of the form:

$$
P(\Delta_{\mathrm{RMST}} > c \mid \text{data})
$$

where $c$ is a prespecified RMST-difference threshold.

For the RMST ratio, users can evaluate a posterior probability of the form:

$$
P(R_{\mathrm{RMST}} > c \mid \text{data})
$$

where $c$ is a prespecified RMST-ratio threshold.

The RMST horizon time is specified by the user. Multiple horizon times may be evaluated when desired. For each horizon, the utility also returns posterior summaries for the comparison-treatment RMST, reference-treatment RMST, RMST difference, and RMST ratio. By default, these summaries report the 2.5th, 50th, and 97.5th posterior quantiles, corresponding to 95% posterior intervals.

## Subpopulation Analyses

Both posterior-probability utilities can optionally restrict the analysis to a specified patient subpopulation.

Subpopulation specifications use the same baseline covariates used elsewhere in the Bayesian-ECD workflow. For example:

```r
subgroup_list <- list(
  sex = "01",
  eor = "0",
  kps = "02",
  age = c(50, 70)
)
```

Categorical variables are specified using codes corresponding to the category order stored in the Bayesian-ECD model, while continuous variables such as age are specified using a lower and upper bound.

For continuous variables, the interval follows the convention:

```text
lower bound <= value < upper bound
```

If no subpopulation restriction is required, the utilities can instead be applied to the full relevant population.

> **Note:** The argument name `subgroup_list` is retained in the R functions for compatibility with the existing code, although this guide uses the term **subpopulation** in user-facing documentation.

## Running the Example

The repository includes a complete example script:

```text
examples/run_posterior_probabilities.R
```

The example demonstrates how to load the required Bayesian-ECD results, source the posterior-probability utilities, specify treatment comparisons and thresholds, and calculate posterior probabilities.

From the repository root, the example can be run in R with:

```r
source("examples/run_posterior_probabilities.R")
```

Users may also open the script directly in RStudio and run individual sections interactively.

The example includes posterior-probability analyses for both the overall population and selected subpopulations.

## Interpreting Posterior Probabilities

Posterior probabilities quantify the posterior evidence that a treatment comparison satisfies a prespecified threshold.

For example, a result such as:

```text
P(HR < 0.80 | data) = 0.95
```

would indicate that, under the fitted Bayesian-ECD model, 95% of the relevant posterior distribution satisfies the specified hazard-ratio criterion.

Similarly, an RMST analysis can quantify the posterior probability that an RMST difference or ratio exceeds a prespecified threshold.

These probabilities should be interpreted relative to the treatment comparison, threshold, time point or RMST horizon, and analysis population specified by the user.

> **Important:** A posterior-probability threshold should be prespecified according to the scientific or decision-making objective of the analysis. The utility reports posterior evidence relative to the criterion supplied by the user; it does not determine what threshold should be considered clinically meaningful.

## Relationship to the Shiny Application

The posterior-probability utilities complement rather than replace the primary Shiny workflow.

The Shiny application provides the main graphical and numerical Bayesian-ECD summaries, including survival curves, hazard-ratio curves, RMST results, subpopulation analyses, and prediction outputs.

The optional R utilities provide additional posterior summaries when the analysis requires an explicit probability statement about a prespecified treatment-effect threshold.

Users who only require the standard Shiny outputs do not need to run these utilities.

# Output Files

The Bayesian-ECD Shiny application provides several options for downloading analysis results. Available downloads depend on the analysis being performed.

## Bayesian-ECD Model Results

The **Plot Output** tab provides an option to download selected Bayesian-ECD model results as a ZIP archive.

The downloaded archive contains:

```text
picube.xlsx
Lognormal_Mu_Cube.xlsx
Lognormal_Sig_Cube.xlsx
Allocation_variables.xlsx
Variable_specifications.txt
```

These files contain selected posterior quantities and model specifications generated by the Bayesian-ECD analysis.

The ZIP archive is named using the date and time at which it is downloaded, for example:

```text
results_YYYYMMDD_HHMMSS.zip
```

This timestamp helps distinguish results generated from different analysis runs.

## Plot Downloads

Plots generated by the application can be downloaded as PNG files.

Download options are available for:

- primary Bayesian-ECD survival or hazard-ratio plots;
- RMST plots;
- subpopulation survival or hazard-ratio plots;
- prediction survival or hazard-ratio plots; and
- the optional concurrent-control compatibility plot.

For plots that provide width and height controls, users may specify the desired dimensions in inches before downloading the figure.

If dimensions are not specified, the primary, RMST, subpopulation, and prediction plot downloads use the displayed plot dimensions. The concurrent-control compatibility plot uses a default download size of 14 × 8 inches.


The saved plots are named using the date and time at which they are downloaded, for example:

```text
plot_YYYYMMDD_HHMMSS.png
rmst_plot_YYYYMMDD_HHMMSS.png
subgroup_plot_YYYYMMDD_HHMMSS.png
prediction_plot_YYYYMMDD_HHMMSS.png
control_compatibility_plot_YYYYMMDD_HHMMSS.png
```

## RMST Tables

The application provides CSV downloads for tabular RMST results where available.

The **Subpopulation RMST Output** tab provides a downloadable RMST table for the selected subpopulation.

The **Prediction RMST Output** tab provides a downloadable RMST table for the selected prediction population.

These tables contain the treatment-specific RMST summaries together with the RMST difference and RMST ratio for the selected treatment comparison.

The saved tables are named using the date and time at which they are downloaded, for example:

```text
data_YYYYMMDD_HHMMSS.csv
prediction_rmst_YYYYMMDD_HHMMSS.csv
```

## File Organization

Downloaded files are saved through the web browser or RStudio viewer used to display the Shiny application. The final download location therefore depends on the user's browser and operating-system download settings.

For reproducible analyses, users should retain the input dataset, analysis settings, and corresponding downloaded outputs together.

When multiple analyses are performed, it is recommended that downloaded results be organized into separate directories or otherwise labeled so that each output can be associated with the dataset and analysis settings that generated it.

# Privacy, Reproducibility, and Local Execution

## Local Execution

The Bayesian-ECD Shiny application is designed to run locally in the user's R environment.

When the application is launched locally using RStudio or:

```r
shiny::runApp("app")
```

the analysis is performed within the local R session.

The application does not require users to upload their analysis dataset to a separately hosted Bayesian-ECD web service.

Users remain responsible for following the data-governance, privacy, and security requirements applicable to their datasets and computing environments.

## Reproducibility

Reproducible use of the application requires retaining both the analysis inputs and sufficient information about the software environment used to perform the analysis.

At minimum, users should retain:

- the version of the Bayesian-ECD Shiny repository used for the analysis;
- the input dataset;
- the column specifications entered in the application;
- relevant analysis settings and selected treatment comparisons;
- any subpopulation definitions used;
- any prediction dataset used; and
- the downloaded analysis outputs.

When an analysis is associated with a scientific publication or other reproducible research workflow, the Git commit corresponding to the version of the application used for the analysis should also be recorded.

For example, the current commit can be obtained from the repository root with:

```bash
git rev-parse HEAD
```

The R session information, including the R version and versions of loaded packages, may also be recorded with:

```r
sessionInfo()
```

The repository does not currently include a package lockfile. Users who require exact software-environment reproducibility should therefore retain the recorded R and package versions used for the analysis.

## Stored Bayesian-ECD Information

The application uses stored Bayesian-ECD posterior components included with the repository under app/data/storedMCMCiter/ as part of the analysis workflow.

These stored components should be treated as part of the computational specification of the application. Analyses intended for reproducible scientific use should therefore identify the repository version used rather than replacing or modifying stored model components without documenting those changes.

## Research Use

When results from the application are used in research, reports, or publications, users should document the analysis population, treatment comparison, time horizon or evaluation time, subpopulation restrictions when applicable, and other settings needed to interpret the reported result.

Citation information for the Bayesian-ECD methodology and this software repository should be included when available.

# Troubleshooting

This section describes several common issues that may occur when installing, launching, or using the Bayesian-ECD Shiny application.

## The Application Does Not Launch

First confirm that the required R packages have been installed as described in the **Installation and Launch** section.

The application should be launched from the repository using:

```r
shiny::runApp("app")
```

or through RStudio.

If an error reports that an R package is missing, install the indicated package and restart the application.

On systems where packages must be compiled from source, additional system build tools may be required. See the installation instructions earlier in this guide.

## The Uploaded Dataset Is Not Accepted

Confirm that the uploaded file is a CSV file and that the column names entered in the **Uploaded Data** tab exactly match the corresponding column names in the dataset.

The model-fitting dataset must provide the information required by the application, including the patient identifier, survival outcome, censoring indicator, treatment, cohort, and required baseline covariates.

Also verify that categorical values use category labels compatible with the levels stored in the historical Bayesian-ECD model, as described in the **Preparing the Current RCT Dataset** section.

## Treatment Selections Are Missing or Incorrect

Treatment choices are populated from the treatment information in the uploaded dataset.

Verify that the treatment column was specified correctly and that the dataset contains the expected treatment labels.

The reference control treatment is expected to be labeled:

```text
Control
```

Pay particular attention to capitalization, spelling, and leading or trailing spaces in treatment labels.

## The Control Compatibility Check Cannot Be Run

The compatibility diagnostic requires concurrent-control patients in the uploaded current RCT dataset.

The concurrent control treatment must be labeled exactly:

```text
Control
```

If no such patients are present, the diagnostic cannot be performed. This does **not** prevent the user from continuing with the primary Bayesian-ECD analysis.

If concurrent controls are present but the diagnostic cannot be run, verify that the treatment column was specified correctly in the **Uploaded Data** tab and that the uploaded dataset was successfully read. At least five concurrent-control patients with usable survival time and censoring information are required for the compatibility diagnostic.

## A Subpopulation Contains Too Few Patients

A selected combination of sex, EOR, KPS, and age restrictions may produce a very small analysis population.

If the selected subpopulation contains zero or one patient, the application will report an error rather than generate the requested result.

Broaden one or more of the selected subpopulation criteria and rerun the analysis.

Remember that age intervals use the convention:

```text
minimum age <= age < maximum age
```

so the minimum value is included and the maximum value is excluded.

## Prediction Data Are Not Accepted

The prediction dataset should contain:

- a patient identifier; and
- the baseline covariates required by the fitted Bayesian-ECD model.

The prediction dataset does not require survival outcomes, censoring indicators, treatment assignments, or cohort labels.

Verify that the required covariates are present and that categorical values are compatible with the category levels stored in the Bayesian-ECD model. The application reports an error when an unseen prediction category is encountered.

## A Plot Does Not Download as Expected

If custom plot dimensions are provided, verify that the width and height values are valid.

If custom dimensions are not required, leave the corresponding fields unspecified. The primary, RMST, subpopulation, and prediction plot downloads will use the displayed plot dimensions, while the concurrent-control compatibility plot uses a default download size of 14 × 8 inches.

The location of the downloaded file depends on the browser or RStudio viewer being used to display the application.

## The Application Becomes Unresponsive During an Analysis

Some Bayesian-ECD calculations may require more computation than ordinary Shiny interface operations.

Allow the current analysis to finish before repeatedly submitting the same request or launching additional analyses.

If the application must be restarted, stop the current Shiny session before launching it again.

In RStudio, this can be done using the red **Stop** button.

## An Unexpected Error Persists

If an error persists:

1. record the exact error message;
2. record which application tab and operation produced the error;
3. confirm that the example datasets supplied with the repository work as expected;
4. record the repository version using `git rev-parse HEAD`; and
5. record the R environment using `sessionInfo()`.

When reporting a software issue, provide this information together with a minimal description of the steps required to reproduce the problem.

Do not include confidential or patient-identifiable data in public issue reports.
